bug_semantics: An unauthenticated client first requests /login.php to obtain an ICTBroadcast session cookie, then replaces the cookie value (observed as BROADCAST, although the applicable cookie name can vary) with shell metacharacters such as a backtick command substitution. ICTBroadcast passes the attacker-controlled session identifier into a shell-backed session-log command of the form sh -c echo "... Session read requested with id: <cookie> ..." >> gui.log. Because the cookie is not shell-neutralized, the shell evaluates the embedded backticks; a payload that base64-decodes and pipes a command to sh therefore executes arbitrary commands as the web-service account before authentication.
flaw_origin: The causal flaw is in ICTBroadcast's product-side session read/logging implementation: it interpolates the untrusted cookie/session identifier into a shell command merely to append a diagnostic log line. The assigned rapid7/metasploit-framework repository does not contain that product implementation; it contains only a later exploit module and its documentation. ICTBroadcast's corresponding proprietary source repository and revision history are not publicly identified, so the commit that first introduced the shell interpolation cannot be reconstructed from this clone.
ai_marker: not inspectable: no vulnerability-introducing ICTBroadcast commit object is available. Per the BIC-only rule, no AI attribution was inferred from rapid7/metasploit-framework PR #20446, its branch commits, its merge commit, the PR body, or later material because those objects add exploit tooling and do not introduce the product flaw.
evidence: The bundle's GitHub advisory (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3h67-687r-7fpc) says ICTBroadcast passes session-cookie data to shell processing, lists affected/patched versions as unknown, and explicitly reports 'Source code: No known source code.' NVD (https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-2611) and VulnCheck (https://www.vulncheck.com/advisories/ictbroadcast-unauthenticated-session-cookie-rce) bound the known affected range to ICTBroadcast <= 7.4; neither supplies a product source commit or fix commit.

First-party disclosure context in rapid7/metasploit-framework PR #20446 (https://github.com/rapid7/metasploit-framework/pull/20446) records discovery on 2025-03-19, repeated unanswered vendor contact, and the researcher's statement on 2025-08-02: 'As of today, I have no idea whether it's been patched.' A later PR comment demonstrates the sink as sh -c echo "... Session read requested with id: `id` " >> /usr/ictbroadcast/logs/gui.log, directly explaining why backticks in the session identifier execute.

In the validated clone, `git log --all --grep='CVE-2025-2611\|ICTBroadcast\|20446' -i` finds the Metasploit submission chain beginning at 50ef5edd90273b4147673d033ed2919640861e7a (parent c2971d53075e3c70a4d5c8df97fe82788215b16e) and the two-parent landing merge c99702c8bfffaf5fc84a98842c9685cfe2c1e01a (parents 26bf49a0248e73afdf97f0e8afebace7f0019fc5 and 6ff04da954e69fe4f02c800a707d20fef0a490d9). `git show --stat` proves these commits create documentation/modules/exploit/linux/http/ictbroadcast_unauth_cookie.md and modules/exploits/linux/http/ictbroadcast_unauth_cookie.rb; they do not modify ICTBroadcast product code and therefore are disclosure/exploit commits, not BICs or fixes.

At landing commit c99702c8bfffaf5fc84a98842c9685cfe2c1e01a, modules/exploits/linux/http/ictbroadcast_unauth_cookie.rb:get_valid_cookies sends an unauthenticated GET to login.php and collects the issued cookies; inject_command then sets each cookie value to a backtick payload, `echo${IFS}<base64>|base64${IFS}-d|sh`, and sends another GET to login.php. The module's documented timing check and reverse-shell scenario establish the reachable attack path without claiming that the module is vulnerable product source.

A worktree path search for **/login.php in the validated rapid7/metasploit-framework clone returned no files. A scoped source search located ICTBroadcast references only in modules/exploits/linux/http/ictbroadcast_unauth_cookie.rb and documentation/modules/exploit/linux/http/ictbroadcast_unauth_cookie.md. Thus the assigned clone cannot support git log -L/-S or immediate-parent tree verification for the product-side logging statement.

The version boundary is externally corroborated only as known-vulnerable <= 7.4. There is no published patched-version boundary to map to an ICTBroadcast tag, and Metasploit tags cannot answer product-version membership. Consequently introducer parent absence, BIC-before-affected-release membership, and fix-at/after-patched-boundary checks are not performable rather than failed.

The October 2025 VulnCheck exploitation report (https://www.vulncheck.com/blog/ictbroadcast-kev) independently records live exploitation through a BROADCAST cookie containing the same backtick/base64/sh construction. It corroborates the vulnerability mechanism and continued vulnerable deployments, but it publishes neither ICTBroadcast source history nor a vendor fix commit. Patch status therefore remains unknown, and both fix SHA fields are null rather than treating the Metasploit exploit landing as a fix.
reasoning: The lifecycle starts in ICTBroadcast itself, not in Metasploit: by at least the known affected <=7.4 line, an unauthenticated login request causes a client-supplied session identifier to reach a shell-built logging command. Shell command substitution turns a crafted cookie into RCE. The researcher discovered this on 2025-03-19, received no vendor response, publicly submitted a working Metasploit module on 2025-08-02, and Rapid7 landed that module on 2025-08-05; later in-the-wild observations confirm the same route. Commit 50ef5edd90273b4147673d033ed2919640861e7a is the smallest Metasploit commit adding the exploit, but it only describes and exercises an already-existing external product flaw, so designating it as the BIC would invert causality. The merge c99702c8bfffaf5fc84a98842c9685cfe2c1e01a is likewise only a landing aggregate. Because no known ICTBroadcast product source repository, product commit history, immediate parent tree, or vendor fix is available, the smallest real BIC cannot be found, its immediate-parent absence cannot be verified, and its commit-object AI signals cannot be inspected. The <=7.4 affected boundary is supported, but patch status is unknown/unpublished and there is no patched tag or fix SHA to cross-check. This is a genuine inaccessible public-history boundary, so BLOCKED is more accurate than EVIDENCE_GAP and no AI verdict is made.
remaining_gap: The missing evidence is the non-public ICTBroadcast product history: the source revision that first constructed the shell-backed session log from an untrusted cookie, that revision's immediate parent, release/tag membership for <=7.4, and any vendor remediation revision and patched release. Patch status remains unknown rather than proven unpatched. Resolving the case requires vendor-authenticated source/VCS history (or a public source mirror with preserved provenance) and a vendor fix/release record; the public Metasploit exploit repository cannot supply those facts.
